## Why?

Quarto's built-in `code-line-numbers` covers the common case: highlight some
lines, optionally step through them. `code-style` is a superset — same
behavior comes out of the `hi` style.

The mapping is one-for-one. Use `code-style` when you outgrow it (custom
colors, multiple styles per step, the diff preset, labels…).

## Range — `code-line-numbers="3-5"`

````markdown
```{.r data-code-style="hi:3-5"}
df |>
  filter(cyl == 6) |>
  group_by(gear) |>
  summarise(m = mean(mpg)) |>
  arrange(desc(m))
```
````

```{.r data-code-style="hi:3-5"}
df |>
  filter(cyl == 6) |>
  group_by(gear) |>
  summarise(m = mean(mpg)) |>
  arrange(desc(m))
```

## Disparate lines — `code-line-numbers="2,4"`

````markdown
```{.r data-code-style="hi:2, hi:4"}
df |>
  ...
```
````

```{.r data-code-style="hi:2, hi:4"}
df |>
  filter(cyl == 6) |>
  group_by(gear) |>
  summarise(m = mean(mpg)) |>
  arrange(desc(m))
```

## Progressive — `code-line-numbers="|3|4-5"`

````markdown
```{.r data-code-style="|hi:3|hi:4-5"}
df |>
  ...
```
````

Press → to walk through.

```{.r data-code-style="|hi:3|hi:4-5"}
df |>
  filter(cyl == 6) |>
  group_by(gear) |>
  summarise(m = mean(mpg)) |>
  arrange(desc(m))
```

## Combined progressive — `code-line-numbers="|2,4|3-5"`

````markdown
```{.r data-code-style="|hi:2,hi:4|hi:3-5"}
df |>
  ...
```
````

```{.r data-code-style="|hi:2,hi:4|hi:3-5"}
df |>
  filter(cyl == 6) |>
  group_by(gear) |>
  summarise(m = mean(mpg)) |>
  arrange(desc(m))
```

## Where `code-style` goes further

You can pick a different color, stack styles, or attach a label — things
`code-line-numbers` can't do:

````markdown
```{{r}}
#| code-style:
#|   styles:
#|     warn: { bg: "#ffd4d4", gutter: "#c00", marker: "!" }
#|   steps:
#|     - hi: 2
#|     - warn: { line: 4, label: "this is the bottleneck" }
```
````

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-style:
#|   styles:
#|     warn: { bg: "#ffd4d4", gutter: "#c00", marker: "!" }
#|   steps:
#|     - hi: 2
#|     - warn: { line: 4, label: "this is the bottleneck" }
df |>
  filter(cyl == 6) |>
  group_by(gear) |>
  summarise(m = mean(mpg)) |>
  arrange(desc(m))
```
